event_context.setup_notes_realized: USGA doubled fairway width vs 2004 and did not adjust green speed or hole locations for wind; R3 scored harder than R1 despite R1 carrying the more severe forecast label
event_context.top_finish_profile_summary: Top 3 finishers (Clark, Burns, Kim) all carried at least one anti-pattern flag; 6 of top 10 finishers carried at least one anti-pattern flag. Tier 1 produced 1 actual top-10 finish (Scheffler) against an average model-implied top10 probability of 70.3%.

venue_changes.new_value: reduce magnitude by ~30-40% when fairway width is materially widened from historical USGA setup AND USGA states no wind-driven green-speed/hole-location softening (i.e. driving demands are the primary lever left, but a wider corridor partially offsets spray penalty)
venue_changes.evidence: Top 2 finishers (Clark, Burns) were both pre-penalty Tier 2 (74.7, 78.2 VTS) and were demoted to Tier 3 specifically by this penalty (-4.0, -6.1 VTS respectively), then finished 1st and 2nd.
venue_changes.confidence_of_change: moderate - single event, but unusually concentrated and directionally consistent across both top finishers
venue_changes.next_audit_checkpoint: re-test at next wide-fairway major or wind-classified US Open setup before making this a permanent venue rule

engine_rule_flags.scope: cross_venue_candidate (needs 2nd supporting event before promotion to engine rule)
engine_rule_flags.issue: Named structural risks (APP_200+ for Rahm/Young, MajorGrind for Henley/Hovland/Cantlay) correctly identified the failure mechanism for 5 of 7 major Tier 1/2 misses, but the named risk did not translate into enough VTS discount to move tier placement or materially adjust probability outputs.
engine_rule_flags.proposed_fix: When a named primary_risk_trait is present AND the live/forecast weather class directly stresses that trait (e.g. wind class + APP_200+ risk, four-round major + MajorGrind risk), apply an explicit secondary discount to top10_pct/win_pct beyond the existing trait-weight penalty, rather than relying on the trait weight alone to carry the full effect.
engine_rule_flags.confidence_of_change: low-moderate - directionally clear this event, needs a second major/high-variance event to confirm before becoming a binding engine rule
engine_rule_flags.next_audit_checkpoint: next major championship or high-wind-classified event

engine_rule_flags.issue: Make-cut probability was badly miscalibrated at both tails: Tier 4 predicted 18.2% avg make-cut vs 43.2% actual; Tier 5 predicted 3.1% vs 26.3% actual; Tier 2 predicted 78.8% vs 50.0% actual. The week was correctly labeled 'high_wind' but the variance-compression rule (scoring spec 8.2) was not applied aggressively enough to make-cut/top10 outputs specifically.
engine_rule_flags.proposed_fix: Increase the variance-driven compression coefficient applied to make_cut_pct and top10_pct (not just win_pct) when venue_variance_class or weather_forecast_class = high. Win probabilities were less obviously miscalibrated (field-wide win_pct summed to 1.0 correctly) but make-cut/top10 bands need the same treatment as win_pct already gets.
engine_rule_flags.confidence_of_change: moderate - clean tail-miscalibration signature, but only one event's worth of evidence
engine_rule_flags.next_audit_checkpoint: next 2 high-wind or high-variance-classified events; compare predicted vs realized make-cut/top10 rates by tier each time before codifying a fixed compression coefficient

engine_rule_flags.issue: Pre-tournament weather forecast ranked R1 as hardest and R3 as second-hardest; actual scoring difficulty inverted this (R3 73.62 > R1 73.28). Minor magnitude but worth tracking if it recurs.
engine_rule_flags.proposed_fix: No rule change yet. Note for future events: round-by-round forecast severity should be treated as a rough guide, not a hard input to round-specific player risk language, until forecast-vs-actual day-sequencing accuracy is tracked across multiple events.
engine_rule_flags.next_audit_checkpoint: track forecast-day-rank vs actual-scoring-day-rank across next 3 events
